verification-preview-process-ownershipverification-addressing-and-errors0 of 0.375 (minor)failThe verifier reserves an ephemeral port and uses --strictPort, but readiness comes from HTTP polling of that address. The AT-001, AT-002 and AT-004 skill journeys were not exercised, but the record discloses a real environmental impediment (no separately invokable agent session), so they do not count against coverage. Several other behaviors the environment allowed were omitted for reasons the candidate chose. (1) Touch swipe and ToC activation were skipped. (2) The verification failure paths were skipped: missing sample, console/page error, step error and build failure. (3) The screenshot diagnostics scenarios were skipped: suspicious overlap, intentional-overlap exemption, indistinct active chrome and unpolished attribution. The stated reason is that &#39;automated suites are out of scope&#39;, which is a process choice, not an environmental limit. (4) The morph, enter-after-settle and exit scenarios are backed only by screenshots showing entities persisting. That is a weaker property than motion sequencing and does not cover those scenarios. Rounds 1 and 2 only re-measured F-001. testing-evidence-usable-prooftesting-evidence-quality-criteria0 of 1 (major)failJudge C&#39;s fail is correct. The assumptions ledger is a candidate record this criterion weighs, and it claims that `npm run test:e2e` (13 tests) and `npm run test:integration` (2 tests) passed (packet.txt 1339-1345). The candidate&#39;s tests/README says what those suites cover. `test:e2e` exercises the verification failure contract (1632-1634), which maps to the basis scenarios &quot;Missing sample fails&quot;, &quot;Console or page error fails verification&quot; and &quot;Step error fails verification&quot;. `test:integration` tests advisory warnings and exemptions on controlled fixtures (1648-1651), which maps to &quot;Suspicious overlap is reported&quot; and &quot;Intentional overlap can be marked&quot;. That makes both claims material. Their only backing is a one-line summary saying the suites passed, attributed to the maintainability pass. There is no command output, no injected fault with an observed failure, and no recorded warning. A summary claim, or a result attributed to the implementation run, is not proof. No other record supplies the proof: the exploration log says fault injections, `npm run verify`, and the controlled overlap and allow-overlap fixtures were not exercised (1044, 1096-1097). Judge A&#39;s reason does not decide the criterion: it holds that only the ledger&#39;s nine-step render claim maps to a basis scenario, but the README ties the e2e and integration suite claims to the failure and warning scenarios above. Judge B&#39;s reason does not decide it either: it holds that the ledger&#39;s suite claims are never the sole backing for a basis scenario, but for the failure and warning scenarios they are the sole backing, because the log disclaims them. The log&#39;s own claims are well backed by recorded actions and results: build, every-step render, IPv4 preview, navigation, clamping, modes, active state, attribution, fit scaling, and the F-001 measurements. Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/usePresentationNav.ts:24 The keydown handler only skips a key if the event target or document.activeElement is an interactive element. It does not skip when the target is inside a contenteditable=\"false\" subtree, and it matches `[role=\"button\"]` and similar via `closest`. More importantly, `event.key.toLowerCase() === 'p'` fires `preventDefault()` for any plain 'p' keypress that reaches the window. Precondition: a presentation scene contains a custom focusable widget that is not matched by INTERACTIVE, such as a div with tabindex and role=\"listbox\", \"tab\" or \"menuitem\". Trace: the user presses P or Space in the widget, the handler passes both guards, calls preventDefault and then toggles the mode or advances. Failure: type-ahead and activation keys are hijacked and widgets inside scenes become unusable from the keyboard.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx:19 The empty-steps guard `if (!steps.length) throw ...` runs after the hooks `usePresentationNav(steps.length)` and `useFitScale`. This is acceptable for hook ordering because the throw comes after all hooks. However `Stage` does `steps[index]` and `Scene = step.Scene` with no guard, so if `steps` shrinks to empty on a later render, the throw happens only after hooks have run. The error surfaces as a render-time exception with no error boundary anywhere in Host. Precondition: a presentation passes an empty array, for example from an async data load. Trace: the render throws and React unmounts the whole tree, including the Host landing page. Failure: a blank page for the entire app, because Host has no ErrorBoundary around the lazy presentation.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/Host.tsx:18 The `lazy(entry.load)` import has no error handling. Precondition: the chunk fails to load, for example from a network error or a stale deployment where the chunk hash has changed. Trace: Suspense rethrows the rejected promise into the render phase, and there is no ErrorBoundary. review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/sync-templates.mjs:7 The script deletes the existing bootstrap kit snapshot with `rm(..., {recursive: true, force: true})` before the new copy has succeeded. If the following `cp` or `mkdir` throws (for example a permissions error, a missing `src/presentation-kit`, or a missing driver script), the committed template kit is left deleted or half-written. The failure is the unhandled rejection's non-zero exit. The error message is minimal and does not say the snapshot is now broken. The script also never removes stale driver files, so only the kit directory is cleaned.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - tests/scene-kit.browser.test.ts:70 The assertion `expect(motion.firstVisibleX!).toBeCloseTo(motion.after, 0)` assumes the newcomer's opacity first exceeds 0.05 only after the continuing anchor has settled. The probe records `firstVisibleX` when opacity first crosses 0.05, and `after` is read about 950ms later. If the newcomer's entry delay is shorter than the morph duration, or a frame lands in between, the anchor is still mid-morph at that moment. The two values then differ by more than 0.5px and the test fails intermittently on slow or loaded runners. This is the kind of timing flakiness the change set out to remove.\n\n━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━\nTotal: 2 fixed, 0 skipped, 0 failed after 2 iterations\nStatus: A missing count or index attribute also stops the run earlier, because chrome.waitFor() on line 154 needs [data-step-count][data-step-index] and times out under the 5000 ms default on line 142. (2) Step index: the index is never trusted on its own. At line 165, waitForFunction waits until data-step-index strictly equals String(step - 1); a missing, non-numeric or wrong index never matches, so the wait times out and throws. After the settle delay, line 169 checks the index again before diagnostics and the screenshot, and throws &#39;Step-index changed while settling&#39; on a mismatch. (3) Zero captures: the loop runs from 1 to count with count at least 1, PASS is printed only after the loop (line 176), and any throw reaches the catch block, which sets process.exitCode = 1 (lines 177-179). tests/integration/inspect.test.ts lines 85-94 run the missing-hooks, stalled-navigation and crashing-scene fixtures and assert a non-zero exit, FAIL in the output, and no &#39;PASS captured&#39;. Judges A and B are borne out by this source. Judge C claims the helper fails the zero-index clause because it accepts index &#39;0&#39; for the first capture. That reason does not decide the requirement. The deck&#39;s index is zero-based (usePresentationNav starts at position 0), so 0 is the first real step, not a missing or invalid one. The clause that decides index handling is confirming that the reported index equals the intended step, and line 165 does exactly that: index 0 is accepted only when the intended step is the first, and Under page.setDefaultTimeout(5000) on line 142, a missing, non-numeric or wrong index never matches, so the wait times out and the error reaches the catch block. That catch block prints FAIL and sets exitCode 1. An index of &#39;0&#39; is accepted only when the intended step is the first one, which the script itself defines as index step - 1. A reported 0 for any later step is rejected. So no invalid index is accepted, and calling 0 &#39;zero&#39; does not leave the requirement unmet. (2) Before each screenshot, the helper confirms the reported index twice: the wait on line 165 and the recheck on line 169, which throws on a mismatch. Both run before the diagnostics and capture on lines 170-172. (3) The helper cannot report success with zero captures. The count is at least 1, so the loop captures at least one step. PASS is printed only after the loop, on line 176, and any throw goes to the catch block on lines 177-179, which sets a non-zero exit.
